before.title: Infotainment Screen Freezing and Bluetooth Drops
before.description: The Venue infotainment system experiences periodic screen freezes, Bluetooth audio dropouts, and slow response to touch inputs. The system occasionally requires a hard reset to recover. Wireless phone connectivity is particularly unstable with certain phone models.
before.solution: Visit the dealer for the latest infotainment software update. For persistent Bluetooth issues, delete and re-pair the phone. A hard reset (hold power button 10 seconds) resolves screen freezes. Switching to a wired USB connection improves stability.
symptoms: Apple CarPlay or Android Auto disconnects

before.title: IVT (CVT) Judder and Hesitation
before.description: The Hyundai Venue uses an IVT (Intelligent Variable Transmission), which is Hyundai's version of a CVT. The IVT can exhibit judder during low-speed acceleration, hesitation when merging or passing, and a rubber-band effect during throttle changes. The transmission programming prioritizes fuel economy, causing noticeable delays between throttle input and vehicle response. Hyundai has released TCM software updates to improve responsiveness for some model years.
before.solution: Confirm the concern with a road test at low-speed takeoff and light-to-moderate throttle, then scan the TCM/PCM for stored or pending transmission-related codes and verify the IVT fluid level/condition using Hyundai service procedure. If no hard faults are present, perform the latest TCM software update/reflash and adaptive relearn, which is the primary fix for delayed response, judder, and rubber-band feel on many Venue models; dealers typically charge about $150-$250 if out of warranty, though many updates are covered under powertrain warranty or service campaign work. If symptoms remain, inspect for contaminated or incorrect CVT fluid, input/output speed sensor issues, or internal belt/pulley wear, with fluid service commonly costing $250-$400 and IVT replacement or overhaul often running $3,500-$6,000.

citations.title: TSB 22-AT-010H: IVT/Smartstream Transmission Control Module Update for Shift Quality and Driveability
NHTSA Complaint #11484934

before.title: EGR Valve Electrical Short Causing Loss of Drive Power - Recall 24V308 (Campaign 260)
before.description: On 2024 Venue (and related Elantra/Kona) models, an EGR valve sensor contaminated with solder flux during supplier manufacturing can develop an internal electrical short. The short can cause a sudden loss of drive power while driving, increasing crash risk. NHTSA recall 24V308 (13,511 units across the three models) was opened in 2024.
before.solution: Free recall remedy under NHTSA 24V308 / Hyundai Campaign 260: dealers replace the entire EGR valve assembly at no charge. Owner notification letters were mailed June 28, 2024. Confirm recall status by VIN at nhtsa.gov or via Hyundai (1-855-371-9460).
symptoms: Sudden loss of drive power / reduced power while driving
Rough idle or hesitation preceding power loss
Active recall flagged on VIN lookup

proposal.solution: Check the VIN for NHTSA recall 24V-308 / Hyundai Campaign 260. Hyundai dealers replace the EGR valve assembly free of charge.

before.title: Engine Stalling / Shut-Off When Braking or at a Stop
before.description: Venue owners, concentrated on the 2020 model, report the engine unexpectedly shutting off, particularly while slowing or coming to a complete stop, sometimes with rough idle. Some cases are traced to a faulty or corroded wiring-harness connector near the battery causing intermittent power interruptions. CarComplaints and YourMechanic both document the slow-down/stop shut-off pattern, with stalling reported at low mileage.
before.solution: Have the dealer inspect and repair the battery/wiring-harness connector and check for stored DTCs and applicable TSBs; corroded or loose connectors should be cleaned or replaced. Persistent stalling the dealer cannot resolve over multiple visits may qualify under state lemon laws. On 2024 models, rule out the separate EGR-valve recall (24V308).
symptoms: Engine shuts off when slowing or stopping
Random stalling while driving / loss of power
No-start or hard-start after the engine dies

before.title: Horn Becomes Weak or Inoperative Due to Internal Corrosion (Warranty Extension TXXU)
before.description: The Venue's horn can become faint or completely inoperative when foreign substances and moisture intrude into the horn assembly, oxidizing/corroding the internal contacts. The failure was common enough that Hyundai issued Warranty Extension TXXU covering the horn assembly on 2020-2022 Venue (QX) vehicles. Horn/electrical failures are a documented complaint pattern for the model (electrical is a top complaint category for the 2022 Venue on CarComplaints).
before.solution: Dealer confirms the horn is inoperable and replaces the horn assembly. Under Warranty Extension TXXU, coverage is extended to 10 years / 120,000 miles from original in-service date for affected 2020-2022 Venue (QX) built 01/11/2019-04/25/2022, so replacement is free within those terms for original and subsequent owners. Out of warranty, horn plus labor is inexpensive.
symptoms: Horn does not sound when pressed

before.title: IVT (CVT) Complete Failure / Sudden Loss of Acceleration
before.description: Beyond low-speed judder, owners report the Intelligent Variable Transmission (a belt/pulley CVT) suffering loss of acceleration or power while driving, sometimes at low mileage. A September 2024 California federal class action (Donadio v. Hyundai Motor America) alleges the IVT in 2020+ gas Hyundais including the Venue can fail to respond to the accelerator, described as a safety hazard, and that the vehicle may not respond even when the accelerator is pressed.
before.solution: Failed IVT units are typically replaced under Hyundai's powertrain warranty (10yr/100k mi); document symptoms and dates for warranty/lemon-law leverage. Some owners report a transmission control software reflash for hesitation, but persistent or complete failures require unit replacement. Affected owners may be covered by the ongoing IVT class-action litigation.
symptoms: Sudden loss of acceleration / no response when pressing the accelerator
Vehicle hesitates or fails to respond under throttle
Feeling that the transmission has disengaged
Transmission failure reported at lower-than-expected mileage

before.title: Rear Backup Camera Fogging and Image Distortion
before.description: The rear backup camera lens accumulates moisture internally, causing foggy or distorted images. The camera housing seal fails, allowing condensation to form on the lens. Occurs more frequently in humid climates.
before.solution: Replace rear backup camera assembly. Ensure new camera mounting gasket is properly seated. Apply dielectric grease to connector. Some owners add additional sealant around the housing edge as preventive measure.

before.title: Seat Belt Pretensioner May Explode in a Crash - Recall 22V458 (Campaign 231)
before.description: On 2020-2022 Venue models, the front driver and/or passenger seat belt pretensioner can over-pressurize and explode when it deploys in a crash, projecting metal fragments into the cabin that can injure occupants. The root cause is excessive internal pressure in the pretensioner pipe during certain crashes. NHTSA recall 22V458 covers roughly 72,470 Venue units and expands/replaces the earlier 21V796 recall.
before.solution: Free recall remedy under NHTSA 22V458 / Hyundai Campaign 231: dealers install a cap that secures the seat belt pretensioner so fragments cannot escape. Vehicles previously repaired under 21V796 must return for the updated remedy. Verify VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls or with a Hyundai dealer (1-855-371-9460).
symptoms: Active open safety recall on VIN lookup
No driving symptom - hazard only manifests during a crash deployment

proposal.title: Seat Belt Pretensioner May Explode in a Crash - Recall 22V458 (Campaign 231)
proposal.description: NHTSA recall 22V-458 covers certain 2020-2022 Hyundai Venue vehicles. The driver-side and/or passenger-side pyrotechnic seat belt pretensioner may deploy abnormally in certain crashes because of over-pressurization. Metal fragments could enter the occupant compartment and injure occupants. The recall report states there is no warning before abnormal deployment.
proposal.solution: Check the VIN for NHTSA recall 22V-458 / Hyundai Campaign 231. Hyundai dealers secure the pretensioner micro gas generator and delivery pipe with a cap to prevent potential abnormal deployment, free of charge.
symptoms: No advance warning before abnormal pretensioner deployment

before.title: Theft Vulnerability - No Engine Immobilizer (Kia/Hyundai Theft Trend)
before.description: 2020-2021 Venue models with turn-key (non-push-button) ignition were built without a standard engine immobilizer, making them easy to steal with a USB cable using a method that went viral on social media. The vulnerability drove a nationwide spike in theft claims. Hyundai responded with a free anti-theft service campaign rather than a formal recall.
before.solution: Get the free anti-theft software upgrade at a Hyundai dealer (rolled out from Feb 2023, takes under one hour); it sets the factory alarm and adds an 'ignition kill' feature so the car cannot start when subjected to the popularized theft method. Vehicles produced after November 2021 already have a standard immobilizer. Check eligibility at hyundaiantitheft.com.
symptoms: Vehicle has a turn-key ignition without an immobilizer (no push-button start)
Broken window or damaged steering column from a theft attempt
Difficulty obtaining or high cost of theft insurance
Targeted in 'Kia Boys' USB-cable theft method

citations.title: Hyundai Introduces Free Anti-Theft Software Upgrade, Beginning With More Than 1 Million Elantras, Sonatas and Venues
Anti-theft software tamps down viral theft trend targeting Hyundai, Kia vehicles - IIHS

proposal.title: Theft Vulnerability - No Engine Immobilizer (Kia/Hyundai Theft Trend)
proposal.description: Hyundai Campaign 993 includes certain 2020-2021 Venue vehicles that are not equipped with an engine immobilizer and are not equipped with a push-button START/STOP ignition. The campaign bulletin explains that many Hyundai vehicles without push-button ignition did not have an immobilizer and could be theft targets; eligibility must be checked by VIN.
proposal.solution: Check the VIN for Hyundai Service Campaign 993. For eligible vehicles, a Hyundai dealer upgrades the Integrated Body Control Unit or Body Control Module software and installs anti-theft decals. After the update, use the key fob to lock and unlock the vehicle to activate or deactivate the anti-theft system, and disarm it with the key fob before attempting to start the vehicle.
symptoms: Vehicle is eligible for Campaign 993 by VIN
affectedSystems: Integrated Body Control Unit / Body Control Module
